question.problem:
The system of equations

$$
\begin{aligned}\{\begin{aligned}-y+z=1 \\ 2z+y+x=-1 \\ 3y-z+x=1\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

can be represented using matrix notation as

$$
[\begin{aligned}a & -1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & b \\ 1 & c & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

What are the values of $a,b$ and $c?$

current_example.problem:
The system of equations

$$
\begin{aligned}\{\begin{aligned}2x-y+z=4 \\ z-x+2=-1 \\ 2y-2x-4z=-4\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

can be represented using matrix notation as
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14130155/assets/08a20165c8f65b5c5f31e8015eedcec1baa10c3bd70d0964a640aee98dab3ea3.svg)
What are the values of $a,$ $b$ and $c?$
current_example.worked_solution:
First, let's write the system so that $x$, $y$, and $z$ appear in each equation in the correct order and all constants are on the right-hand side of the system:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2x-y+z=4 \\ -x+0y+z=-3 \\ -2x+2y-4z=-4\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can write the system in the form $A\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b},$ where

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14130155/assets/143c9c6e7fdb3772f1ad4b44ce5461893ca5b99ce0a72b7ec41b5d78db8643f8.svg)

is the coefficient matrix,

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14130155/assets/ee6b50d3e909fb379649c9859124b6633319008d978cb94940828659c29152ee.svg)

is the column vector of constants, and

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14130155/assets/bf8ebfa7ea9ec71d8cad0c8effb986eb734179b2e5aa208ae8bc6afd231d90ba.svg)

is the column vector of variables.

So, the equation $A\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b}$ becomes

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14130155/assets/03124c054d9c5de6d00cf7404d2ef1ea17cc5174d3a743d318f323963c39bd93.svg)

Therefore $a=0,$ $b=-2,$ $c=-3.$
